The group escapes with a fortune in loot and no losses, leaving the tree undefeated and a mysterious, unopenable black chest as the one thread carried into book three.

recaps.text: In the first Hell Difficulty Tutorial, an ordinary young man named Nathaniel Gwyn is pulled from a commuter bus, along with a crowd of strangers, into a lethal fantasy 'tutorial' governed by a game-like system of levels, skills and status windows, and set to the deadliest difficulty, 'Hell.' Detached and calculating, he survives the first floor's monster-choked trials by building himself into a fragile but devastating mana specialist, losing an arm and killing the apex predator that hunted them as his friend Kevin dies. On the war-torn second floor the survivors are scattered and treated as low-status outsiders; Nathaniel kills a noble who threatens him and is taken in by an ancient, near-omnipotent woman known as the Master and her attendant Ruby, who becomes a genuine friend. As that floor ends, the Master reveals herself as Lissandra, an 'absolute' who believes she is an artificial creation of the system, kills Ruby and destroys a city, then sacrifices her own body to erase the second floor's world so Nathaniel can witness it. He escapes alone to the third floor and reunites with Isabella, the young sister of Sophie, the woman who once secretly tampered with his mind. The rest of the group survives but is broken into scattered clusters, and the healer Lily lies unconscious, having given up her own arm to restore his.

On the third floor, a vast, decaying, monster-filled city, Nathaniel and Isabella begin alone at level 75, hunting diseased giant rats and far deadlier named monsters while searching for the rest of the group. Water and food, not combat, prove to be the floor's real threat. Reaching out over the survivors' message board, Nathaniel is reassured by Tess that his core memories are intact, but grows increasingly suspicious that Sophie's earlier tampering erased more than he realized. He and Isabella rescue a trio of weaker survivors who transferred up from the easier 'Hard' difficulty, chiefly the calculating, water-creating Cipher, on strictly transactional terms. They also find a family of the floor's frightened natives, who explain the setting: generations ago a corrupting force called 'decay' turned monsters and people alike into undead-like horrors and collapsed the food supply, and the surviving city grew up inside a protective field created by a figure called the Saint, a field that is slowly failing. Nathaniel, meanwhile, keeps remaking his own body and mana, and begins deliberately loosening his rigid emotional control when Isabella is nearly killed in front of him.

Drawing on what he saw of Lissandra at the second floor's end, Nathaniel builds new internal mana constructs, including one fused to his own heart that turns each heartbeat into raw force, nearly killing himself before he stabilizes it. Hunting alone, he is cut off from the group and relentlessly pursued by two powerful undead 'mage hunter' monsters whose attacks cancel a mana-user's skills, exactly the sort of enemy his fragile, mana-heavy build fears most. Badly wounded, he finally kills both and collapses outside a shelter, only to wake to Sophie healing him and reflexively break her nose. The reunions cascade from there: Sophie, Tess and Aaron are already together, and soon Lily and Kim rejoin as well. Lily, still missing the arm she sacrificed for him, heals him at cost to herself, and the two reconcile. Nathaniel studies her technique to build a healing skill of his own, thanks Kim for having protected her, and confronts Sophie about his memories, which she does not deny. By now most of the scattered survivors are back together, with only Hadwin, Maya and Dennis still unaccounted for.

As the group travels deeper toward the city's center, Nathaniel keeps training and killing ever-stronger monsters. Lily reveals her own brutal close-combat style, a grey-mana strike that eats away flesh and shuts down enemies' self-healing, and pushes herself hard despite her injuries. Nathaniel reaches level 100, unlocking a gradual body upgrade that reduces his need for food, water and sleep, and hunts and kills alone a house-sized undead deer far above his level with a single overcharged, self-made explosive attack. He and Tess, it emerges, are both quietly chasing something the rest of the group is not: a token that would let them step into a difficulty even harder than Hell, and Nathaniel combines two of his tokens as a step toward it. Leaving the native survivors behind, and at Lily's insistence handing them the group's precious sparrow trap, the survivors press on and finally come within sight of the floor's great wall: an immense, smooth, seamless white structure threaded with visible mana, towering over the entire city.

The uneasy alliance with the transferred survivors ends in blood: Goldie uses a hidden hypnotic ability on Nathaniel, and while his emotional control is stripped away he kills both her and Cipher, having learned they were scheming to seize Lily as a captive healer. Regaining himself, he reconciles with Lily, and near the wall the whole group finally reunites when Hadwin, Maya and Dennis rejoin. The group scales the great white wall and, on the far side, battles a set of enormous undead beasts kept there long ago as a ruler's 'pets': they kill a second house-sized undead deer, and Nathaniel alone grinds down a monstrous undead bear that unnervingly mimics his own heart-construct. Along the way an old, itching mark on his restored left palm resolves into a hidden circuit shaped exactly like the Peacemaker, the powerful defensive item Lissandra gave him. Unsettled, he deliberately severs his own left hand to investigate it.

The severed hand regrows into something new: a small, breathing, flesh-and-bone form that speaks and calls itself Lissandra, an imprint of the ancient being's mind left inside the Peacemaker. Unable to take him over, it strikes a bargain to correct his mana technique in exchange for one day carrying a message to her original self's home world. Under its harsh coaching Nathaniel undergoes brutal 'active tempering,' pounding his own body with force to make it stronger at agonizing cost, and merges two of his skills into one, which finally fulfils the last condition for the token he and Tess have been chasing. He steps into 'Beyond,' a difficulty above Hell entered only briefly once every few months: a one-hour survival trial against swarms of Cinderbears and poisoned, invisible goblins that pushes him to his limit. He clears it, and a vast presence briefly overrides the system to single him out with a cryptic warning never to let a skill reach its ninety-ninth level.

Nathaniel spends a hard-won reward to permanently double his mana pool, then struggles with the enormous imbalance it creates, building a fourth construct that renders his own mana untouchable by outside interference. Between training the whole group and drawing closer to them, he keeps the Lissandra imprint's counsel but never lets it near his body work. When it is finally time to move on, he memorizes the coordinates to her original's world, destroys the record, and, after the imprint spends the last of its power in a final overwhelming display, burns it to nothing. A system-wide announcement declares an 'irreversible narrative progression' has begun and shuts off the survivors' message board. The group crosses a second, blue wall into a pristine, eerily lifeless inner city where nothing decays, and is met by an extraordinarily powerful, unstable swordsman who calls himself a warrior of the last king, protector of what he names the last bastion of humanity, his level far beyond anything the group can read.

The warrior hosts the group under a courteous but explicit death threat, confining them to a deserted mansion until an audience with his king. The inner city, its king and its three warriors turn out to be thousands of years old, frozen and undying inside the Saint's preservation field. At the audience the king bluntly announces he will kill them all, sparing only Lily as a healer, and confirms Nathaniel's guess: the Saint is long dead, her body kept artificially 'alive' to sustain the field, and the 'decay' bleeds from her death. Nathaniel springs a hidden weapon, instantly killing two of the three warriors; in the battle that follows, the near-invulnerable king regenerates from any wound until Nathaniel forms a strange black mana blade, severs the king's link to the Saint, and kills him. The group loots powerful items from the dead. Then a piece of Lissandra, secretly planted inside Hadwin's arm, regrows into a second, mana-less but physically overwhelming incarnation of her.

The reborn Lissandra effortlessly overpowers the group, wounding several and costing Lily an arm again, but the real Lily, sacrificing most of her own limbs, lands a decisive blow that finally destroys the Saint's body and clears the third floor. Portals open to the fourth floor for the tutorial's survivors but not for Lissandra, who is left behind. On the new floor the group finds a shop, a currency of 'shards,' and a subclass system; Nathaniel chooses his subclass and refuses to spend his tokens on shortcuts, preferring to earn mastery himself. Camped in a cold mountain range, the survivors puzzle over a field of artificial-looking debris orbiting the planet and bottomless holes bored into the mountains, before discovering that the mountains themselves are a vast colony of giant ants. The group narrowly escapes a huge swarm and reaches open plains, with the fourth floor's main quest set before them: destroy one of its four 'calamities.'

While the rest of the group settles into a distant, inhabited city, Nathaniel returns alone to the ant mountains to grind levels and decompress. The colony fights back like a coordinated army, throwing wave after wave of specialized ant variants, joint barriers and counter-tactics at him, and he adapts each time, favouring concentrated fire, the one thing the ants resist worst. Wanting only a few more levels before a class upgrade, he drops a compressed mana-and-heat bomb down one of the bottomless tunnels and flees; it sets off an enormous underground chain reaction that kills ants for hours and rockets him from level 146 to 159 in a single stroke, far past what he intended. Shaken, he swears off the mountain range for weeks. Meanwhile, in the nine days apart from him, the group has bought a fine city house with the proceeds of their third-floor loot and built a working base, intelligence network and hunting routine of their own.

Reaching the city, Nathaniel learns its 'surprise': it is ruled by the Lynthari, a long-lived, far higher-levelled race of cat-featured people who treat humans roughly the way humans treat cats, and who find his composure and mismatched eyes fascinating. He takes a level-150 class upgrade, and his stored 'reservoir' of surplus mana keeps swelling toward triple his main pool. The central conflict of the previous book finally resolves when Sophie, in a raw exchange, asks him for a genuine clean slate rather than payment, and he agrees; the two begin a scheme to repeatedly sell Lissandra's world coordinates to the system shop for a fortune in shards. The group registers a small guild and maps the city, learning that four 'calamities' loom over the floor: a giant ant colony, a dead champion's corpse puppeted by an ancient armor, an immense sickly tree in the ruined old capital, and a fourth of which nothing is known. Life, for once, is comfortable, and Nathaniel quietly admits he wants more of it.

That comfort ends when Elydor, guildmaster of one of the city's major guilds, forces his way into the group's home, humiliates them, and coerces them into a dangerous expedition as expendable support, alongside a second major guild led by the more cautious Obelia and a smaller guild used as fodder. The target is a dead champion's manor in the ruined old capital, held by a calamity-tier giant, sickly tree of terrifying power. The raid succeeds, and the group hauls out treasure including a heavy, lockless black chest, but as the expedition retreats the tree throws up a barrier sealing the entire city, trapping everyone inside. For roughly three weeks the tree kills off the guilds one by one with a silent, near-undetectable attack that slowly turns victims into plant matter; the smaller guild is wiped out entirely and several of Elydor's people die. The group survives intact only because Nathaniel secretly and continuously shields them the whole time, at real physical cost and by suppressing his own emotions to endure it. Once he has learned everything he can from the two guilds' failed attempts to break the barrier, he drops that suppression and turns on Elydor.

In a single lopsided battle, Nathaniel and the group kill Elydor and his elite fighters, holding back only enough to keep their own people safe; Sophie uses her mind control lethally for the first time, Lily kills with her disintegration touch, and Biscuit, now manifesting solid mana tentacles, finishes Elydor off. Obelia keeps her own guild out of the fight and stands down when Nathaniel challenges her, parting on wary but respectful, transactional terms and warning that Elydor's death will bring political fallout. Nathaniel then crafts an item that finally cracks the tree's barrier, and the survivors escape by emergency teleport, landing near the ant mountains, where ants are unsettlingly seen moving outside their territory for the first time. Back at their city base, the group divides an enormous haul, including five powerful items most of which Nathaniel claims or shares out. Every member of the group and Biscuit is alive and unharmed; Elydor's guild and the smaller one are destroyed, while Obelia's guild and the Lynthari remain standing and cautiously friendly. Two of the floor's calamities are still untouched and the sickly tree survives, its barrier visibly expanding. The book closes on one unresolved mystery, a black chest from the manor that resists every skill anyone in the group has, including Lily's disintegration, which Nathaniel vows to open however long it takes, and on a quiet moment as Biscuit returns his signature nose-boop for the first time.

characters.description: The book's first-person narrator: a detached, calculating young man with heterochromia (one grey eye, one brown) who has cleared three prior floors of the lethal 'tutorial' on its hardest 'Hell' difficulty. He opens the third book as the undisputed power center of his reunited band of survivors, now settled in a fourth-floor city, leveraging his strength into guild politics while running relentless, physically dangerous experiments on his own mana and body. Fierce about protecting the people he counts as his own, he holds most others at arm's length behind rigid emotional control.
characters.name: Nathaniel Gwyn

characters.description: Sophie's much younger sister, around ten, and Nathaniel's near-constant companion since the previous floor. A fire-based fighter, blunt about violence yet unusually perceptive of others' feelings, she is openly devoted to Nathaniel and needles him out of his isolation. Early in the book she is given her own point-of-view chapter, and she keeps up a running, affectionate rivalry with him over the group's telepathic corgi.
characters.name: Isabella Martinez

characters.description: Isabella's older sister and a powerful manipulator of minds and emotions. Fully reconciled with Nathaniel after the previous floor's 'clean slate,' she now works closely with him, including on a scheme to sell a stranded ancient ally's world coordinates through the system shop for a fortune. Her mind control meets little resistance from this floor's natives, making it quietly one of the group's most dangerous tools.
characters.name: Sophie

characters.description: One of the people Nathaniel has known and trusted longest, and among his closest allies: a fierce fighter who wields lightning and self-guided javelins. Calm and quietly persuasive, she helps run the group's day-to-day operations and is one of the few people Nathaniel opens up to. Like him, she privately pursues entry to 'Beyond,' a trial difficulty even harder than Hell.
characters.name: Tess

characters.description: The group's primary healer, fully recovered since the previous floor, who also fights with a terrifying disintegration touch that few enemies survive. Gentle but relentless, she continues a patient, openly stated romantic interest in Nathaniel that he neither accepts nor firmly refuses, and pushes herself hard to grow strong enough to stand at his side.
characters.name: Lily Chen

characters.description: One of the group's steadiest hands, anchoring its logistics alongside Tess, whose drilled, watchful bearing suggests a law-enforcement past. His body-strengthening skill has grown so potent he can casually overpower armed, mana-using attackers unharmed. Gruff and physically tough, he carries an old, complicated history with Nathaniel that has long since settled into loyalty.
characters.name: Hadwin Harper

characters.description: A diligent survivor who fights with controllable projectiles that slow whatever they strike, and one of Nathaniel's training partners. Earnest and eager to grow stronger, he works to overcome a tendency to freeze under pressure, and over the book comes into his own as one of the group's most formidable members.
characters.name: Kim Min-Jae

characters.description: The group's telepathic corgi, under Nathaniel's sworn protection and increasingly autonomous. He communicates in single telepathic words, fights with manifested mana tentacles, and has grown steadily stronger; Nathaniel and Isabella keep up an affectionate rivalry over his loyalty. His signature exchange with Nathaniel is a shared nose-boop.
characters.name: Biscuit

characters.description: A warrior of the Lynthari, the cat-featured, long-lived race that rules the fourth floor and regards humans roughly the way people regard cats. High-levelled and fixated on Nathaniel and his mismatched eyes since the group's arrival on this floor, she spars with him, has gifted him rare items, and hovers close to his group with a protective, proprietary interest that sets her apart from her aloof kin.
characters.name: The Lynthari Warrior

characters.description: A capable fighter of the group who works with self-made mana armor and shape-shifting weapons. Off the battlefield she reveals an unexpected softer side, taking up the violin again after abandoning it years earlier over a painful adolescence she recounts with dark humor.
characters.name: Maya

characters.description: A small white snake with emerald eyes, hatched early in the book from a mysterious beast egg and belonging to Isabella. Of an unrevealed ancient bloodline, it grows noticeably larger over the floor and becomes another focus of doting attention within the group.
characters.name: Noodle

characters.description: The guildmaster of one of the fourth-floor city's five major guilds: a short, battle-eager, stone-natured fighter who answers Nathaniel's open invitation to spar at a meeting of the city's guild leaders. Unlike her more hostile peers, she comes away from the beating friendly rather than resentful, declaring him a promising future sparring partner.
characters.name: Isola

characters.description: The guildmaster of another of the city's five major guilds, known to the group since the previous floor's expedition as calmer, more professional and more perceptive than her peers. She seeks Nathaniel out personally at his group's house, preferring direct dealings to intermediaries, and shapes up as one of the city's more valuable potential allies.
characters.name: Obelia

characters.description: The ruling matriarch of the Lynthari, the fourth floor's dominant native race, revealed to be the same eccentric socialite who had earlier tried to buy the group's telepathic corgi. Ancient and immensely powerful, she presides over the city's guilds and holds knowledge of the planet's hidden past that reframes the floor's calamities.
characters.name: Eris

characters.description: The leader of the ant Colony, one of the fourth floor's calamities: a matte-black, light-absorbing ant with wings of mana and thousands of visible mana threads running to every ant under its command, its level completely unreadable. Intelligent and disturbingly ego-driven, it leads the assault on the city in person and singles Nathaniel out with an open, mocking challenge.
characters.name: The First One

characters.description: The reborn incarnation of an ancient, near-omnipotent being who guided and tested Nathaniel on earlier floors and once sacrificed herself for him. Stranded since the previous floor, she reappears in person near the end of the fourth floor. She claims a history of past disciples and carries a severed arm belonging to another being of her own extraordinary rank, both of which she leaves unexplained.
characters.name: Lissandra

characters.description: A six-year-old half-demon child, with small horns and red eyes, assigned to Nathaniel as his charge at the start of the fifth floor, where the quest is to raise and protect a disciple. A starved, guarded survivor of a ruined world, she is fiercely self-protective at first and responds better to transactional trust-building than to kindness; under Nathaniel's harsh but devoted mentorship she slowly grows into an affectionate, increasingly capable student. He gives her a name partway through their time together.
characters.name: The Disciple

characters.description: Nathaniel's first significant native contact on the fifth floor's ruined, monster-overrun world: a wary survivor reached over a looted communicator, suspicious that the stranger on the line is connected to the deaths of his own people. He questions Nathaniel closely, sets careful terms for an items-for-medicine trade, and insists on verifying the story before extending any trust.
characters.name: Darren

characters.description: Darren's second-in-command at the fifth-floor survivor bunker, a skilled blade-fighter who serves as Nathaniel's main liaison and guide there. More openly forthright than her leader, she helps arrange Nathaniel's work with the bunker and its long-sealed workshops.
characters.name: Nina

characters.description: A single, extraordinarily dangerous monster stalking the fifth floor's ruined world, far taller and stronger than the lesser human-derived creatures overrunning the dead city, its level unreadable even to Nathaniel. Blade-armed and patient, it is first seen catching three skilled, cloaked survivors and slowly eating them alive while Nathaniel watches without intervening. What it is and what drives it are unknown.
characters.name: The Veil Guardian

recaps.ending: Book three ends on the fifth floor, roughly midway through Nathaniel and his disciple's allotted time together, with the rest of the group scattered across separate instances and never reunited on-page after the floor split. The fourth-floor calamities are settled: the Living Tree and the ant Colony are destroyed, the armored Fallen Hero is killed by the group without Nathaniel, and several rival guildmasters are dead. Hadwin is the book's only major loss, killed defending Sophie and the twins. Nathaniel's closest Lynthari ally, feared at real risk of dying once he left, instead survives under the protection of the reborn ancient being, their future together left open. On the fifth floor Nathaniel has raised his half-demon disciple from a starved street child into a devoted student who has just chosen her first class; he has fought the monstrous Veil Guardian to a near-fatal standstill without killing it, and forced a native bunker's hidden cannibalism into the open, freeing its captive victim. The two arrive, at the very end, at a colossal fallen sky-fortress with a dense mana 'valley' beyond it, both unexplored. Left open for the next book: the fortress and the valley; the Veil Guardian's survival and motive; the group's eventual reunion; the mysterious voice and its 'ruler of greed'; and the true nature and purpose of the disciples each survivor now protects.
recaps.in_short: Established as the strongest presence in the fourth floor's city, Nathaniel Gwyn trades a public promise to kill the 'Living Tree' calamity for guild peace, learns the ruling Lynthari are ancient invaders, and watches their matriarch spend her life destroying the tree. When the ant Colony assaults the city, his ally Hadwin is killed and Nathaniel loses a hand; he then hunts the Colony's leader off-world and annihilates the hive by dropping an ancient orbital structure onto it, clearing the floor. His group settles old scores, killing two rival guildmasters and a third calamity, before the fifth floor separates every survivor onto their own instance with a single task: raise a disciple. Assigned a starved six-year-old half-demon girl on a ruined, monster-ridden world, Nathaniel bonds with and trains her, fights a monstrous 'Veil Guardian' to a bloody standstill, and exposes and ends a native bunker's hidden cannibalism. The book closes as he and his disciple, now freshly classed, reach a colossal fallen sky-fortress with a mana-dense valley beyond, both unexplored.

recaps.text: In the first two books, an ordinary young man, Nathaniel Gwyn, is pulled with a crowd of strangers into a lethal fantasy 'tutorial' run like a game of levels, skills and status windows, and locked to its deadliest setting, 'Hell.' Detached and calculating, he survives the monster-choked first floor by building himself into a fragile but devastating mana specialist, losing an arm and watching a friend die. On the war-torn second stretch he is taken in by an ancient, near-omnipotent woman who trains him, then reveals herself as an artificial 'absolute,' destroys her own world to let him witness the truth, and dies. Reunited afterward with the scattered survivors, among them the young girl Isabella and her mind-bending sister Sophie, who had once secretly tampered with his memory, Nathaniel fights on: he helps end the millennia-old guardians of a decaying city, unlocks a trial difficulty beyond Hell, and reaches a fourth floor ruled by the cat-like Lynthari, where his group builds a comfortable city base and his power swells enormously. Coerced by a guildmaster into a deadly expedition, the group is trapped for weeks inside a calamity-tier tree's barrier while rival guilds are wiped out; Nathaniel secretly shields his own people the whole time, then kills the guildmaster once it is safe. The group escapes rich and intact, leaving that tree undefeated and an unopenable black chest as the mystery carried forward.

Now one of the strongest presences in the fourth floor's city of Virelia, Nathaniel turns his reputation into leverage, publicly promising to personally kill the immense, sickly 'Living Tree' calamity in exchange for months of political peace among the city's guilds. He tests his closest Lynthari ally in a real fight, meets the city's rival guildmasters, and openly admits to having killed the guildmaster who trapped his group on the previous floor. A childhood flashback reveals that his sister, Victoria, not he, had killed their abusive father. The group's members finalize their new 'subclasses,' Isabella choosing one built on kindness and Sophie one built on greed, and Nathaniel and Sophie perfect their scheme to sell a stranded ancient ally's world coordinates through the system shop for a fortune. Lily discloses a long-hidden truth about a friend's death on the first floor, lifting guilt Nathaniel had carried for years. A new cross-difficulty community tournament is announced, and the group's fortunes, for once, look secure.

Chasing power beyond the ordinary, Nathaniel enters the second trial of 'Beyond,' a difficulty harsher than Hell: a week of survival with no mana regeneration against a sense-corrupting force. He clears it alone, and during it a mysterious disembodied voice contacts him for the first time, remarking on his subclass and referencing a censored figure it calls 'the ruler of greed.' He emerges with two of his skills fused into more powerful forms. The group learns it can pledge its rare loot as collateral for effectively unlimited Lynthari loans, turning its wealth into a weapon of its own. A mysterious beast egg hatches into Noodle, a small snake of unknown ancient bloodline that attaches itself to Isabella. Tess, too, forges a combined skill and clears Beyond's first trial. As the promised calamity hunt nears, the ancient and immensely powerful matriarch of the ruling Lynthari appears before the group in person for the first time, her knowledge of the planet's past hinting that the floor's calamities are older and stranger than anyone assumed.

An expedition into an ancient mine goes wrong when the group is sealed inside a buried vault. There they fight and destroy a guardian construct, an 'Arcane Archer' imprinted with the personality of a long-dead champion's disciple, in a hard, drawn-out battle. As the construct falls, the mysterious voice speaks to Nathaniel a third time, and the recovered core of the guardian still holds a fragment of personality that resists every attempt to read it. The detour surfaces a troubling theory circulating among the city's guilds: that the Lynthari are not the planet's natives at all but ancient invaders, and that the floor's calamities, the Living Tree, the ant Colony, and a dormant armored champion, are relics left over from a forgotten war. Nathaniel files the idea away, increasingly certain that the truth of this world runs far deeper than the guild politics playing out on its surface.

The vault's ancient array points toward the origin of the ant Colony that looms over the floor, deepening Nathaniel's suspicion of a hidden history beneath the city. Amid the preparations, the group works the city's markets and a major auction, converting loot into wealth and gear ahead of the promised calamity hunt. But the plan to hunt the Living Tree on the group's own terms is overtaken by events: as they ready themselves, the immense calamity abruptly vanishes from its place in the ruined old capital, an impossible disappearance that throws the city's guilds into alarm and turns the whole situation from a planned expedition into a sudden, unpredictable crisis. Nathaniel, who had staked his political standing on personally killing the tree, is left to reckon with a threat that has slipped its leash.

The vanished Living Tree resurfaces as a direct danger, and the truth of the planet comes out with it. The Lynthari matriarch, revealed to be the same eccentric socialite who had earlier tried to buy the group's corgi, confirms the invasion theory: her people are not native to this world, and every Lynthari who knew the secret was killed to keep it. Rather than let the calamity run loose, she destroys the Living Tree herself, spending her own life to do it, and deliberately weakens a kin-controlling power beforehand so no enemy can seize it after her death. One of the city's guildmasters is exposed as a traitor implicated in an earlier killing among the Lynthari. In the aftermath Nathaniel's closest Lynthari ally is left as the people's de facto successor, and the matriarch's quiet farewell message reaches Nathaniel alone, closing a chapter of the floor's politics even as a greater threat, the ant Colony, begins to stir.

The ant Colony erupts into open war on the city. Over a punishing campaign the group fights waves of specialized ant variants; Nathaniel gains a second personal 'trait,' the group deepens its dealings with the city's Craft Guild, and Kim Min-Jae receives a mysterious transplanted 'eye' that sharpens his gravity powers. The Colony reanimates the Living Tree's corpse and hurls it at the city, and Nathaniel and Tess destroy the reanimated husk. Then the Colony's leader, 'the first one,' leads a direct assault on the city itself. In the desperate defense Hadwin is killed shielding Sophie and the twins from the creature, the book's single great loss and the emotional turning point for the group's second half. Nathaniel loses a hand in the same fight while isolating and gravely wounding the Colony's leader, driving it into retreat. Drained to nothing, he resolves to finish the creature no matter where it flees.

Without goodbyes, Nathaniel slips away from the grieving group to hunt the Colony's wounded leader to its source, taking only his closest Lynthari ally with him; the rest of the survivors, steadied by Tess, begin rebuilding and training on their own. The chase leads off the planet's surface to an ancient orbital structure built by the Lynthari's own long-vanished 'absolute,' a derelict now falling toward the city. Repairing an ancient array to reach it, Nathaniel and his ally corner 'the first one' and kill it by redirecting the plummeting structure straight into the Colony's remaining forces, wiping out the hive in a single catastrophic stroke. With the ant calamity destroyed, the fourth floor's main quest completes and the portal to the fifth floor opens, though two of the floor's calamities still stand and the group is not yet whole again.

In the fourth floor's final stretch the group settles its outstanding scores. The ancient orbital base's origins are pieced together; two rival guildmasters are killed, Isola by Nathaniel's Lynthari ally, and Obelia in a revenge raid led by Lily and Tess after she was sent to seize Lily. Lily's subclass is confirmed as one built on wrath. Without Nathaniel, the group hunts and destroys the floor's armored 'Fallen Hero' calamity entirely on its own, Tess driving a lightning spear through its heart. Nathaniel and his closest Lynthari ally share a final farewell duel before he steps alone through the portal to the fifth floor. Behind him, the ancient ally who once died for him reappears in person for the first time in ages and, rather than let his Lynthari companion die now that he has gone, takes her in as a companion and disciple of her own.

The fifth floor is Hell difficulty proper, and its quest is unlike any before: each survivor is separated onto their own instance and told to raise and protect a single disciple. Nathaniel is assigned a starved, guarded six-year-old half-demon girl, with small horns and red eyes, on a ruined, post-apocalyptic world overrun by human-derived monsters and stalked by one far deadlier blade-armed hunter, a 'Veil Guardian' of unreadable level whose nature is a mystery. Through a looted communicator he makes cautious first contact with the world's native survivors, trading with their wary leader and later dealing with a woman who answers in the leader's place. Bit by bit he draws the frightened child out and, learning she never had a real name, gives her one. His harsh, patient mentorship begins turning a self-protective street survivor into a devoted student, even as the ruined world's dangers press closer.

Granted entry at last to the survivors' hidden bunker, an underground refuge sheltering thousands, Nathaniel discovers his disciple carries a rare innate 'kinetic demon heart,' a second power source he begins helping her strengthen. He spends the days crafting gear for her and himself and teaching her to sense mana without her eyes, while she opens up about a childhood of starvation and a flight through a monster-filled forest before the system found her. Working through the population math of the bunker, he realizes its food supply cannot possibly match the number of mouths it feeds, and quietly resolves to learn why. Stonewalled by the eccentric local healer he presses for answers and, having his skin painted with a black-mana training circuit to reach a more central facility, covertly infiltrates a sealed tunnel beneath the bunker. There he finds the horror behind the arithmetic: a captive, endlessly regenerating healer, chained and repeatedly mutilated so his flesh can be harvested to feed the survivors above, who eat it without knowing its source.

Nathaniel confirms that 'the Veil' covering the world was built ages ago by an ancient guild, then deliberately provokes and fights the Veil Guardian head-on. He inflicts near-crippling damage, destroying an arm, blinding an eye, shattering its jaw, but cannot land a killing blow; he loses a leg freeing himself from its bite and survives its final hunt only by suppressing all mana and enduring his own body being crushed in total silence. The Guardian lives, badly wounded, its purpose still unknown. Recovering, he refuses to bury the bunker's secret: he forces its leader to confess the truth to the entire population and personally frees the captive healer, giving him full choice over his own fate; the healer proves to be the father of the local granny-healer who had tended the disciple. As the bunker collapses into turmoil, Nathaniel and his disciple leave for good. She reaches level twenty and chooses her first true class, a kinetic channeler. The book ends on arrival rather than resolution: the two fly north and reach the wreck of a colossal fallen sky-fortress, once home to tens of thousands, with an intensely mana-dense valley glimpsed just beyond it, both entirely unexplored as the story closes.
